transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because water has leaked onto the floor near your plug sockets, this is an electrical hazard. Do not use any socket that looks wet or has been splashed. Regarding the leak: the most common cause of a dishwasher leaking water onto the floor is a faulty door seal (gasket). If the rubber seal around the door edge is split, flattened, or has something stuck in it, water will spray out during the wash cycle and pool on the floor. Another possibility is that an item in the rack is blocking the spray arm, deflecting water at the door. To help narrow this down:
1. 2. Open the door and look closely at the rubber seal around the tub opening. Check for splits, tears, or food debris caught in it.
3. Also check that nothing in the bottom rack is hanging down too low or blocking the spray arm from spinning freely. Please let me know what you find with the seal.

its still running tho!! theres loads of bubbles coming out the bottom of the door and the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. should i just turn it off at the wall?? the socket is right next to it

Do not touch the plug or extension lead if they are wet. The 'loads of bubbles' you see coming out of the door suggests the machine is foaming up because the wrong detergent was used (like washing-up liquid). This foam expands and escapes, looking like a leak but actually being suds. Once it is safe to do so (switched off at the wall), please check: did you use standard dishwasher tablets/powder, or something else? And are there still bubbles coming out when you open the door now?
ok i turned it off. we ran out of tablets so my housemate squirted fairy washing up liquid in. tub is full of suds when i opened the door

The bubbles are most likely from the washing-up liquid. Because water has leaked onto the floor near your plug sockets and extension lead, this remains an electrical hazard. Do not use any socket or extension lead that looks wet or has been splashed. You must have a qualified electrician or appliance engineer check the safety of those sockets before using them again. 1. With the power off, scoop out as much suds as you can from the tub and floor (use old towels).
2. Once the worst of it is gone, plug the machine back in only if the socket area is completely dry and safe to do so.
3. Please let me know once you've cleared the foam and whether the machine runs normally afterwards.
